about.lead: More than four years building software that actually reaches production. Mobile apps with Flutter, web apps with Next.js, and the work of tying them together.
about.p1: I'm from Honduras. Trained as a Systems Engineer, working as a Full-Stack Developer. I build mobile apps with Flutter and web apps with Next.js, React, and TypeScript. I test each product with the tools that fit its stack —from Cypress and Playwright to Vitest, Pest, Jest, and Flutter Test— because I'd rather catch problems before the user does.
about.p2: I studied Systems Engineering at José Cecilio del Valle University and hold certifications in Full-Stack Development and Computer Science. Day-to-day, I work with Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini: they help me move faster, but the architecture calls are mine.

petlab.tagline: An e-commerce with cash on delivery and a complete management panel, for a Honduran pet store.
petlab.short: E-commerce and inventory management for a pet store.
petlab.description: Online store and admin panel for a pet-products business in Honduras — catalog, cart, cash-on-delivery checkout, and inventory with a kardex. TALL stack (Laravel · Livewire · Filament), bilingual ES/EN.
body: PetLab HN is the online store of a nationwide pet-products business in Honduras. The challenge wasn't just selling online: it was running a real business — catalog, inventory, supplier purchasing and orders — from a single system, priced in lempiras with cash on delivery.

I built the storefront on the TALL stack (Tailwind, Alpine, Laravel, Livewire): a filterable catalog, a cart that validates stock when the order is confirmed, checkout with address and map location (Leaflet), customer accounts, reviews and a wishlist. Behind it, a full Filament admin runs inventory with a kardex, purchasing, orders, promotions and reports. Everything is bilingual ES/EN and operates with exact monetary precision in lempiras.
A single codebase covers both the customer-facing store and internal operations — backed by 359 Pest tests and 47 Playwright scenarios.

equine.tagline: An interactive 3D atlas of the equine digestive system, built for veterinary students.
equine.short: Interactive 3D atlas of the horse's digestive system.
equine.description: An interactive 3D model of the equine digestive system — seven labeled organs, click-to-focus, and detailed anatomical notes. Built for a veterinary library.
body: The equine digestive system is unusual — a small stomach, an enormous cecum and colon where fiber ferments. Textbook diagrams flatten all of that into static cross-sections that are hard to read in space.

This atlas puts the whole tract in the browser as a real-time 3D model. A semi-transparent horse silhouette gives anatomical context; the seven organs are color-coded and selectable — by clicking the model directly or picking from the side panel — with names in Spanish and English plus detailed descriptions.

I modeled and labeled the organs in Blender, exported an optimized .glb, and rendered it with React Three Fiber and Three.js. The result runs smoothly on desktop and tablet — a study tool a veterinary student can actually rotate, zoom and explore.

prizio.tagline: Price comparison for Honduran supermarkets · six chains on one screen, built in Flutter for iOS and Android.
prizio.description: Cross-platform price comparison app. Scan barcodes, compare prices across chains, set alerts, and build smart shopping lists.
body: Honduran supermarket chains don't publish comparable prices, so the same product can cost noticeably different amounts from one store to the next, and shoppers have no practical way to know before they go.

Prizio closes that gap. An automated scraping pipeline collects prices from six chains (La Colonia, Walmart, Más x Menos, Paiz, Diprova and PriceSmart); scan a barcode in-store or search from home, and every price shows up on the same screen. Price alerts, price trends and smart shopping lists round it out.

Built for iOS and Android and currently being reactivated. Firebase maintains synchronization and 54 active Cloud Functions, Sentry captures errors, and 3,389 verified tests cover the Flutter app, FastAPI backend, and Functions.

folium.tagline: Academic services platform for Honduran students · a bilingual SEO blog with 40 articles and a 27-service catalog.
folium.short: Academic services platform with SEO-first content.
folium.description: Academic services platform with a bilingual MDX blog (40 articles in Spanish and English), a 27-service catalog, and WhatsApp and email contact flows.
body: Folium Labs offers tutoring, research methodology, data analysis and academic editing to university students in Honduras. The site has to explain every service clearly enough that a student can decide before writing in, and rank for the questions those students actually search.

I built it on Next.js 16 with a typed catalog of 27 services, a bilingual MDX blog (40 articles in Spanish and English on thesis writing, APA and research methods), pages for each university, and contact flows through WhatsApp and Resend email.

Content, pricing and the catalog compile at build time, with no CMS. Consent-aware analytics, schema.org structured data, and 488 unit tests plus Playwright end-to-end flows keep it stable as it grows.

printshop.tagline: E-commerce and back office for a Honduran sublimation business · storefront, admin, invoicing and inventory.
printshop.short: E-commerce with admin dashboard and invoicing.
printshop.description: E-commerce platform with admin dashboard, React-PDF invoicing, Zustand-powered state, and end-to-end inventory management.
body: PrintShop 504 sells custom sublimation products in Honduras: t-shirts, bags, mugs and custom designs. The business needed an online store customers could order from and, behind it, a single place to run products, orders, customers, suppliers and invoicing.

I designed and built the platform on Next.js with Supabase handling auth, data and storage. The public storefront covers catalog, cart and checkout; the admin dashboard adds role-based access, PDF invoices with React-PDF, inventory with low-stock alerts, promotions, shipping, suppliers, Excel reports and an activity log.
Built solo. 707 Vitest unit tests and 330+ Playwright end-to-end tests cover checkout, permissions and every admin module.

arca.tagline: Five-language site for a non-profit · blog, gallery, programs and donations.
arca.description: Non-profit website with blog, gallery, program pages, donation details, and full localization across Spanish, English, French, Portuguese, and German.
body: Since 1977, El Arca Honduras has built communities in Tegucigalpa and Choluteca where people with and without intellectual disabilities share life together. Its supporters and volunteers come from many countries, so the site has to speak to all of them.

I built it on Next.js in five languages (Spanish, English, French, Portuguese and German) with a blog, a photo gallery, program pages, an FAQ, a contact form, and a donation section with the organization's bank accounts.
Every string lives in typed translation files and pages are generated statically, backed by 69 unit tests and 73 Playwright end-to-end tests.

pharmacy.tagline: Internal pharmacy system · rebuilt as a Laravel API and an Angular SPA.
pharmacy.description: Internal pharmacy operations system — inventory with low-stock and expiry alerts, invoicing with tax, register, reports and user roles. Rebuilt as a Laravel REST API and an Angular SPA.
body: Hedman Garcia Pharmacy needed one system for the whole counter: products with stock and expiry dates, invoicing with Honduran sales tax (ISV), the register and reports, with each staff member seeing only what their role allows.

I built it end to end: role-based authentication, invoicing with ISV, stock adjusted on every sale, low-stock and near-expiry alerts, register management and operational reports. It was my first production system, back in 2023.
I later rebuilt it as a Laravel REST API (Sanctum, Spatie permissions) and an Angular SPA on MySQL, backed by 222 Pest tests and Playwright end-to-end flows for invoicing.
